title: Stratified perfect description of the integral completed category
statement: Use the coefficient conventions of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and schemes of [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Here noetherian means that $T$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, finite-dimensional means a finite bound on the lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets, and invertible means that $\ell\cdot1$ is a unit in each local ring. Put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the following conditions are equivalent: (i) $K$ belongs to [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], including its compatible etale-origin witnesses; (ii) there is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] such that on each stratum $K$ is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $A_T\otimes_A^L P$ for a perfect $A$-complex $P$, meaning a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules; (iii) $K$ is bounded and every cohomology sheaf, after a finite stratification, is pro-etale locally $A_T\otimes_A N$ for a finitely presented $A$-module $N$. These conditions also describe exactly the category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] whenever that notation is used over such a $T$, with the same completed ring sheaf and reduction functors. This full subcategory is closed under shifts, cones, standard truncations and cohomology sheaves placed in degree zero.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1; Proposition 6.6.11; Proposition 6.8.11(1),(3). Adapted to the explicitly retained compatible etale-origin witnesses and uniform reduction bounds of the DAG; those clauses must be verified, not identified by notation.

proof.text: The completed local-perfect criterion gives (i) iff (ii), with exactly the retained uniform towers and compatible etale witnesses.

Assume (ii). Apply the realization and local-restriction comparisons to each perfect local model. The scalar lemma makes its cohomology finitely presented, so these give (iii) on the same strata and covers. The perfect-strata uniform-bound lemma supplies global boundedness, including the empty-scheme case.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3); Definition 6.5.1 for the detailed coefficient convention

proof.text: For any sheaf M satisfying the local-module condition in (iii), the valuation ring is a PID. The scalar lemma represents each local module N[0] by a two-term finite free complex. The realization and local-restriction single comparisons therefore make M[0] stratified perfect, hence in (i) by step 1.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3); Definition 6.5.1 for the detailed coefficient convention

proof.text: Now assume (iii). The bounded cohomology cone-witness theorem assembles K from shifts and successive cones of its cohomology sheaves. Step 3 puts these sheaves in (i); uniform-complete triangulated and isomorphism closure put K there. Step 1 also yields (ii).

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3); Definition 6.5.1 for the detailed coefficient convention

proof.text: For the detailed notation under its own coefficient hypotheses, use the projection-normalized coefficient comparison. Finite-torsion and intrinsic constructibility both mean finite locally constant stalks on a finite constructible locally closed partition. The uniform-reduction criterion therefore identifies their reduction conditions, including the common interval, normalized local models and compatible etale witnesses. Intrinsic completeness identifies K with its quotient completion and supplies its Roos triangle. Conversely the detailed Roos triangle makes K isomorphic to that limit; the Koszul comparison and completion reflector make it intrinsically complete. Only the limit-object identification is needed, with no uniqueness assertion for a lift of its projections.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3); Definition 6.5.1 for the detailed coefficient convention

proof.text: Shifts and cones follow from uniform-complete triangulated closure. For truncations, use (i) iff (iii): good truncation retains the allowed cohomology sheaves or replaces them by zero and preserves boundedness. This local-module property contains zero and is invariant under isomorphisms by composing local realizations. The same test applies to H^q(K)[0], whose sole possibly nonzero cohomology is H^q(K). Thus both truncations and all degree-zero cohomology objects satisfy (i).

Old step 3: the PID half of the scalar node plus the single comparisons. Old step 4: the existing cone-witness plus uniform-complete-triangulated. Old step 5: the new coefficient node plus uniform-reduction-criterion, which states the tower models and compatible étale origins (the base pointed to a non-existent 'step 6'); completeness via constant-completion-equivalence, the Koszul Roos-triangle node and the reflector, checked in both directions.
